claims.claim: Reviewers report that the tutorial is unhelpful and poorly designed for teaching game mechanics.

citations.review_text: Not for me. I dont like it. Five different ways to parry and the tutorial is miserable. Very unfriendly towards new players.

The combat is glorious and the most fulfilling from any game I've ever played. It’s like rock-paper-scissors mixed with "two for flinching," at least on the surface. The interplay of the various elements and mechanics is glorious, and it feels rewarding to master.

But you probably won't master them. I've been playing this game effectively since its release and I can tell you this: levels 0–100 are generally considered the learning curve just to grasp the basics. The Tutorial is hot garbage that doesn't teach you any of the true essentials, assuming a new player even plays it. There’s very little reason to do so beyond the gold bonus you receive for completion.

If you want to learn the basics, you need someone to teach you. Things like swing manipulation, accels, drags, chambers, or even ripostes are misunderstood by some players.

Dueling and team fighting require entirely different skill sets. Being good at one will not automatically make you good at the other.

The Devs don't know how to balance team skill either. They ought to take the average level of every player on the server and then try to create two teams with an approximate combination of skill. This is why only 26 people were on the server at a time when the game was free.

Players have complained about "team stacking for ages," but it's a myth. At the time of writing, team selection has been disabled. Teams get crushed more thoroughly now than they ever have before. This shows us that the issue wasn't that good players would join the same team to win games previously. Instead, simply using autoselect at the start without any true balancing mechanism would lead to this situation. Now, as a level 218 player, I can't even swap to the losing team to try and balance things myself.

The Devs don't play their own game. The Devs don't moderate their own community. They don't push content at anything close to a reasonable speed, and if something's broken, expect at least 6 months of sitting on the busted issue …

Never made it out of tutorial 15 minutes of deep dive mechanics . Too much info to digest to the point i'd even forgotten what the instructor asked me to do it was so long winded. Keep it simple why does every single franchise try to re invent the wheel?

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the PvP multiplayer as heavily populated by experienced high-level veterans, creating an extremely steep and punishing learning curve for newer players.

citations.review_text:
If you’re looking for a medieval combat game with incredible mechanics and zero pay-to-win nonsense, Mordhau is a great time, especially if you enjoy PvE.

I have spent the bulk of my time in Horde mode, which has been a blast. The directional combat system feels super rewarding once you start getting the hang of parrying, swinging, and managing your footwork. Being able to build out your own custom mercenary with different armor tiers, weapons, and perks using a point system is also a huge plus.

I also managed to dip my toes into a few PvP matches, and honestly, the veterans are just on another level. Many of them have thousands of hours in the game, so expect to get schooled if you jump straight into PvP as a newer player. That said, contrary to what some people say, I haven't run into any toxicity in chat so far and everyone I've played with has been chill.

Overall, if you want a deep, skill-based slasher and don't mind sticking to Horde mode while you learn the ropes (or just to have fun), it’s definitely worth picking up.

Pros:
• Deep, satisfying melee combat mechanics
• Great point-based character and loadout customization
• Horde mode is a ton of fun for newer players
• Zero pay-to-win mechanics

Cons:
• PvP is dominated by hardcore veterans, making for a steep learning curve for new players

The game can be fun for a few evenings with friends, but expect to die [b]a lot[/b], especially as a new player. There’s no proper skill-based matchmaking, so even at level 1, you can find yourself fighting players who are level 200+.

To actually win fights, you often have to abuse broken or unintuitive game mechanics to gain an advantage. Instead of feeling like you’re improving through skill and practice, it can feel like you’re learning how to exploit the game’s mechanics — which isn’t particularly fun.

Fun with friends, but the experience for new players is rough.

Next game you guys make like this you need to add more PvE game modes. At least if you want to extend the game's lifespan and give newer players a chance to play something too without being pwned by sweat lords of the deep basement. And have PvP modes where bots can fill in for players too with adjustable difficulty. Private matches with bots is another way too.

When it's good, it's some of the most fun melee combat out there 100%, but unfortunately, getting to those moments means wading through a brutal learning curve, sweaty veterans, and enough chaos to make improvement feel optional.

MORDHAU is actually a really good game, and I can see why people loved it when it first came out back in April 2019. The combat is fun, the weapons feel good, and the whole medieval chaos thing is still really cool.
The problem is trying to get into it now. Most of the people still playing are level 200 to 300 with thousands of hours, usually like 3k to 5k, and they already know every weird combo and animation trick in the game. A lot of it does not even feel like normal combat anymore. It feels like they are abusing stuff that was never really meant to be used that way.
It would not be so bad if the community was chill, but a lot of the high-level players are toxic too. They will farm new players all game, but if you manage to kill them one time, their ego completely explodes. You can tell some of them take it way too personally.
The game itself is good, and I honestly wish I got to play it when everyone was new. But now it feels like the veteran players made it almost impossible for new players to enjoy or stick around.

[h1]The Sword Remains Sharp, But the Arena Grows Quiet[/h1]

🎮 When [b]MORDHAU[/b] launched back in April 2019, it felt like a revelation. A medieval slasher that promised brutal 64-player battles, deep swordplay, and the kind of chaotic warfare that makes you feel like a real mercenary. The Kickstarter campaign generated massive excitement, and the game exceeded expectations in the early days. But what happens when you arrive at the battlefield years after the war has ended?

[h2]⚔️ A Masterclass in Melee Combat[/h2]

Let me be direct - the combat system in [b]MORDHAU[/b] is still one of the finest ever created for a multiplayer game. The depth here is extraordinary. 🎯 Every swing of your sword carries weight and consequence. The directional attacks, the parry system, the ability to chamber incoming strikes, morph your attacks mid-animation, and feint to bait reactions - this is not a simple hack-and-slash. This is a martial art disguised as a video game.

🎨 The customization system deserves praise as well. Create your mercenary from a massive selection of armor pieces, helmets, weapons, and cosmetics. Want to be a plate-armored knight with a zweihander? Done. A lightly armored skirmisher with a crossbow? Easy. A ridiculous lute-wielding bard who somehow kills everyone? Also possible.

🔊 Sound design amplifies every hit. The thud of a mace connecting with armor, the ring of steel on steel, the screams of dying mercenaries - the audio landscape creates genuine atmosphere. Each weapon feels distinct in your hands.

[h2]📊 The Grim Reality of the Current State[/h2]

Here is where my optimism meets cold truth. 📉 According to [url=https://steamdb.info/app/629760/charts/]SteamDB data[/url], the game peaked at over 60,000 concurrent players at launch. As of late 2026, you will find roughly 600-700 players online at any given time. The arena is not empty, but it is sparse.

claims.claim: Combat mechanics allow players to manipulate swing timings and animations in ways that look unnatural or resemble exploits.

citations.review_text: Like Chivalry before it, this game has all the aesthetics and feeling you'd want out of a first person medieval combat game. Unfortunately it also has the same backwards and mentally deficient hitbox manipulation and light character spam attacks. Sometimes the combat really works and you find yourself in a duel with someone where it comes down to you being able to just parry and feint back and forth till one of you slips up and looses, but that is so incredibly rare that suffering through playing this game is not worth it. If a man fully armed in plate mail can be killed by someone poking him at arms length with a dagger, then the game is busted. (I understand that people could defeat armored foes historically by tiring out, overwhelming, or grappling them to sink blades through gaps, that ISN'T the same as what happens in game where someone just stands there and pokes at you.) This game's style and ambience are great with many redeeming qualities, but there are foundational issues that are easily and commonly abused that make most fights NOTHING like what one should expect from a medieval combat game.

I'd like to give this game a positive review, but I just cannot. Why?

Cons:
- Broken mechanics: They call it "swing manipulation" because they don't want to admit it is downright cheating.
- Useless builds: Wether you are a heavy armoured knight or an archer, it won't matter, because the "swing manipulation" renders all of the character builds pointless.
- Cheaters/hackers: The game is filled to the brim with those, and the devs refuse to do anything about them.
- The devs: Speaking of devs, they are fully aware of the cheaters and the "swing manipulation" and they refuse to do anything to fix their game. And now the game itself is dying. Congratulations, devs. You ruined a perfectly good game.
- The worst people on Earth: Sometimes you get locked in a map with the most immature, toxic, tryhard, rude, racist, sorry excuses for human beings and the server admins aren't doing anything about them.
- The community: The community is a complete utter pool of smelly garbage. No one is friendly towards new players.
- Random kicks for no reason at all: You get kicked from a server if you show a little bit of skill, because people with a skill issue can't stand being defeated once.

Pros:
- Fun gameplay, when the game isn't filled with cheaters.
- Medieval era.
- Decent amount of maps.
- Nice game modes.
- Large amounts of armours and weapons to choose from.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game has a very high skill ceiling and a steep learning curve, requiring hundreds of hours to master the mechanics.

citations.review_text:
The core gameplay is very good, directional and timed melee system with a very high skill ceiling, but some limits to mitigate animation abuse and so on. Plenty of gear to choose from, as well as perks, to make your fighter how you want them to be. A frail longbowman? A heavily armoured knight with a short range weapon? A moderately armoured infantryman with a polearm?

But, sadly, the high skill nature of the combat means that at this point, almost only the sweatiest players remain. So you either get annihilated in combat for hundreds of hours until you reach their level, or don't play. And judging by the player numbers, most choose to not play. That is on top of mod abuse diminishing the already small community.

A fantastic game, but the moderators and the developers have driven it into the ground, sadly.
Fun, dynamic slasher that doesn't take itself too seriously. Huge skill cap means you can learn the game nd the techniques in it for a long time.
Best melee combat. High skill ceiling and fun community

After 1,400+ hours, I can confidently say that Mordhau is a one-of-a-kind game. I've played plenty of multiplayer games over the years, but none have offered the same level of freedom, expression, and unpredictability that this game does.

The combat system has an incredibly high skill ceiling. Its also one of the biggest hurdles: expect to get destroyed for a long time. This isnt a game where you master the mechanics in a weekend. It takes hundreds of hours before you will even notice your first real improvements, and thousands before you begin to understand the depth of the combat. If youre looking for instant gratification, this probably isnt the game for you. But if you enjoy mastering difficult mechanics, the journey is incredibly rewarding.

One of Mordhaus greatest strengths is how diverse the gameplay can be. You can play as a heavily armored knight, a duelist, an engineer, an archer (JK dont play archer :D), or completely ignore conventional builds and become the guy doing backflips while punching people to death. You run into fist-only acrobats, bow thieves who spend entire matches stealing enemies bows, bards playing music in the middle of a battlefield, roleplayers, trolls, and players who invent completely unique fighting styles. No two matches ever feel exactly the same.

The community deserves its own mention. Yes, it is often toxic. But its also weirdly entertaining. The chat can be absolute chaos, and you can meet some of the funniest, most memorable, and most unhinged people in online gaming. Whether thats a positive or a negative depends on your tolerance for internet culture, but it certainly gives the game personality.

The random moments are what keep me coming back. One second youre locked in an intense duel, the next youre witness a group of players throwing stones at a poor guy, chasing someone with a frying pan, or witnessing an entire frontline collapse because a naked dwarf somehow distracted half the enemy team. Six years ago, I probably would've wrote a glowing review for this game. But after those six long years of playing this game, I fully realize now that this game was in its prime when no-one knew what they were doing. We still remembered how to not take this game seriously in the slightest and just have fun. The writing was on the wall when veteran players started offering "coaching" in exchange for real money. In my eyes, the playerbase completely lost the plot for why most of us got into this game in the first place after that.

In the game's current state, I cannot with any honesty or integrity recommend this game to a fresh player. Do I still enjoy playing this game and have some of the best memories of my life in it? Absolutely, but you are not me. You don't have 2.5k hours of blood, toil, tears, and sweat under your belt. If you jump into this game now, you are going to get your teeth kicked in A LOT. Trying to learn and get better while going up against the players that still stick around in this game is going to be a very hard lesson in how you can do everything right and still lose, and that's not your fault, that's just the reality this game finds itself in now.

I still consider this the superior game compared to Chivalry II, but one aspect that I must concede that Chivalry II does better than Mordhau is "Dumb Fun". Ways to provide yourself with brevity and comedic relief to alleviate the feeling of having someone's digital boot constantly stomping on your face. This key aspect I feel has been slowly withering away as time goes on in the life of this game.

Do yourself a favor, spend the 30$ on something you know you'll enjoy from the start like a meal from your favorite restaurant or a trip to the movies with your partner. Anything really that you can enjoy simply for what it is, and not for what it can potentially be.
hard to get into because most of the playerbase is seasoned vets who will absolutely destroy you but still fun

Unfortunately, Mordhau is in a rough spot today. The player base is small, and the only players left are absolute sweat lords who have mastered every mechanic, making it pretty brutal for new players.

That being said, when this game was at its peak, it was truly something special. For such a small development team, they created a masterpiece. The massive team battles were absolute chaos, and there was nothing else quite like fighting alongside your brethren in the middle of a full scale medieval battle. Some of my fondest gaming memories came from those moments, fighting side by side with your squad, holding your ground as enemies slowly surrounded you. The combat was satisfying, the battles felt alive, and even things like catapults and archers had their place without ruining the melee focused experience.

Mordhau had so much potential, and it’s sad to see where it ended up. I wouldn’t recommend it to a brand new player today, but I’ll always cherish the years when this game was at its peak.

Peak Mordhau: 10/10
Current Mordhau: 3/10

If the developers ever make a Mordhau 2, I’ll buy it day one.

This may be the hardest review I've ever had to write. I love this game. As the "Hours played" can attest, it gave me a lot of happy memories, especially during the stress of the pandemic lockdowns. But I can't in good conscience recommend it to new players as of summer 2026.

Basically, this is and always has been a hard game to get good at--I don't think I ever reached that point--and between new players staying away due to that learning curve, intermediate players falling away from the attrition of time, and both groups being kept away by a lack of updates (I think it's been almost two years since the last update now), the game is left with ghost town servers filled only with the top-tier players. A nice enough bunch, for the most part, but they are SO frustrating to play against because they're just that good.

If you want to take a stab (heh) at the remaining elite-tier players, I wish you luck. I also wish you could have seen this game at its peak. 

Farewell, Mordhau. <Raises blade in one final salute>
